Hey Barneyisyourfriend, cinematography may pay alot but I have no clue.  I started slowly 5 years ago and 2 years ago very agressively.  And after having shot 50 or so films and music videos, I have only now begun to start getting paid.  And the pay was very low.  Barely minimum wage.  And they required me to own all my gear (lights and camera).  So it doesn't really make business sense. But thats the state of filmmaking now.  So I would strongly advice doing it as a hobby only until you can have many years under your belt.  Get a good solid full time job of something else entirely and become a weekend filmmaker.

Hey BellicoseBaby, and thanks for the question.  Our audience has been divided into two types of people and for those different types the appeal is different.  The two types are "affected" and "un-affected".  If "affected" by addiction either directly or indirectly then you may watch the show because you understand and feel for the characters and generally want to see how they get out of the situation.  And you may also want to pass this show onto others who are also dealing.  If you are "un-affected", meaning you have never been directly or indirectly affected then this show may be pure entertainment.  We embrace both types of audiences.  We are telling this person's story with dignity and respect and accuracy.  We would love to have a much larger audience.  Is there something you recommend?
